doc.title: Chico Hamilton interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, January 30, 2000

title: Closing remarks and thanks
summary: He offers to bring his group to the school; goodbyes.

story.theme_name: Thanks and goodbyes: closing the interview
story.community_name: Closing thanks and goodbyes at the end of the interview

blocks.x: Well you have some great philosophies and it’s refreshing—
It’s time to get out of Dodge, right?
It’s time to get out of Dodge. It’s refreshing to hear your ideas and interesting that you’re a forward thinking person.

I sort of pride myself on it. I mean at least being contemporary. I don’t know what’s going to happen tomorrow but at least, hey man, I’m willing to give everybody a shot. Really. In regards to hey, well, maybe I don’t dig it but hey it’s got to be five o’clock somewhere.

You know what I mean? It’s just like when you take a drink at ten o’clock in the morning, right, it’s five o’clock somewhere in the world. I enjoyed this man, so hey, listen man, I want to come up to the school man and play. I want to bring my group up and play. I want to get something a little different in from what you’re going to hear every day.
All right. I’ll check into it.
